description: Six-panel composite of SEM fractographs of Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C low-density steel tensile specimens annealed for 1 h at 800 °C (a,b), 900 °C (c,d) and 1000 °C (e,f); each panel is stamped top-left with its letter and top-right with its condition ("800 °C, 1 h", "900 °C, 1 h", "1000 °C, 1 h"). The low-magnification panels (a,c,e) carry a 100 µm scale bar and show strongly banded, layered fracture surfaces in which horizontal secondary cracks, labelled "secondary crack" with blue arrows, run parallel to the banding. The high-magnification panels (b,d,f; 10 µm, 10 µm and 25 µm scale bars) resolve the local fracture modes, with blue labels reading "secondary crack", "ductile fracture" (dimpled areas) and "quasi-cleavage fracture" (flat facets/river patterns). Panel (d) shows the largest dark secondary crack and the most prominent dimpled ductile region; in (f) the dimpled region is smaller and less distinct. Together the panels show that fracture in every specimen is a mixed ductile-plus-quasi-cleavage mode with well-developed banding-related secondary cracks, and that the ductile contribution weakens from 900 to 1000 °C. No numeric data values are printed on any panel.

subfigures.description: Low-magnification SEM fractograph of the 800 °C, 1 h specimen (100 µm scale bar): strongly banded/layered fracture surface with a horizontal dark open crack annotated 'secondary crack' by two blue arrows.

High-magnification SEM fractograph of the 800 °C, 1 h specimen (10 µm scale bar) with three blue labels: 'secondary crack' (upper right, dark crack), 'quasi-cleavage fracture' (centre, flat facet) and 'ductile fracture' (lower left, dimpled area).
Low-magnification SEM fractograph of the 900 °C, 1 h specimen (100 µm scale bar): banded fracture surface with a dark horizontal secondary crack annotated 'secondary crack' with two blue arrows.

High-magnification SEM fractograph of the 900 °C, 1 h specimen (10 µm scale bar): a large dark secondary crack at the top annotated 'secondary crack', a prominent dimpled 'ductile fracture' region at left and a 'quasi-cleavage fracture' region at the bottom.
Low-magnification SEM fractograph of the 1000 °C, 1 h specimen (100 µm scale bar): banded fracture surface with secondary cracks annotated 'secondary crack' with two blue arrows.

High-magnification SEM fractograph of the 1000 °C, 1 h specimen (25 µm scale bar) labelled 'secondary crack' (top), 'quasi-cleavage fracture' (centre-right) and 'ductile fracture' (bottom); dimpled area appears smaller than in (b) and (d).

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a low-magnification SEM fractograph of the 800 °C, 1 h specimen with a 100 µm scale bar, showing a strongly banded, layered fracture surface with a horizontal secondary crack marked by two blue arrows.

Panel (b) (800 °C, 1 h, 10 µm scale bar) carries three blue annotations: 'secondary crack', 'quasi-cleavage fracture' and 'ductile fracture', i.e. dimpled and flat-faceted regions coexist on the same fracture surface.
Panels (c) and (e) (900 °C, 1 h and 1000 °C, 1 h) are low-magnification views with 100 µm scale bars showing the same banded morphology and 'secondary crack' annotations as (a).

Panel (d) (900 °C, 1 h, 10 µm scale bar) shows the largest dark secondary crack of the three high-magnification panels together with a clearly dimpled 'ductile fracture' area and a 'quasi-cleavage fracture' area.

The high-magnification panel (f) (1000 °C, 1 h) uses a 25 µm scale bar (larger field of view than the 10 µm bars of (b) and (d)) and its labelled ductile dimpled region is the smallest and least distinct of the three.

No numeric data values, axes or composition labels are printed in any of the six panels; the only quantitative markings are the scale bars (100 µm, 10 µm, 25 µm) and the annealing conditions stamped in the panel corners.
The caption states that the fractographs are of specimens annealed at (a)(b) 800 °C, (c)(d) 900 °C and (e)(f) 1000 °C.

The citing text states that large secondary cracks are well developed in all specimens according to the low-magnification fractographs (a), (c) and (e), and that these cracks are believed to be related to the banded microstructure.

The citing text states that fracture at 800 °C is a mixed mode of ductile fracture and quasi-cleavage fracture, the dimpled area produced by ductile transgranular fracture of γ and the river pattern by quasi-cleavage of α phase, with κ-carbide at matrix and grain boundaries contributing to cleavage fracture from grain boundaries.

The citing text states that at 900 °C and 1000 °C the fracture mode is predominantly a mixture of ductile fracture of γ phase and quasi-cleavage fracture of α phase, and that the ductile fracture area in the 900 °C specimen (Fig. 17(d)) is more obvious than in the 1000 °C specimen.
The citing text states that the SEM fractograph (Fig. 17(e) and (f)) shows the ductile fracture area has already lessened and becomes not apparent in the specimen annealed at 1000 °C.
The citing text states that the effect of boundary κ-carbide along some large α grains on the fracture of the 900 °C and 1000 °C specimens cannot be obtained from Fig. 17(c) through (e).
